home.meta: Infiniti reads a book or a course, links people and ideas into an interactive graph, and ties every relation back to the source text.
home.freeTitle: Type any person or topic and grow a relation graph
home.freeDesc: Type any person or study topic. The system pulls reference articles and lays out a 3D graph along a timeline.
home.peopleExamples: Try Su Shi, or grade-3 math
home.tagline: An AI reads the material, links people and ideas, and keeps every relation tied to the source.
home.step3: Follow a relation to the source
home.import: Import a textbook, notes, or technical docs and grow your own graph
home.searchFull: Search a person, idea, or topic (try 诸葛亮, 勾股定理, 颜回)
home.footerPartial: {{ready}} / {{total}} materials are ready · the rest are still being prepared
home.footerAll: {{count}} materials · import a textbook, notes, or technical docs to grow the same kind of graph
home.credit: Texts from 5000yan · textbook from Smart Education of China · images from Wikimedia Commons

graph.subtitle: Study graph
graph.preparingSub: The text is being fetched, relations extracted, and the galaxy built. This view will open when that finishes.

explore.maxNodes: The canvas has reached {{max}} nodes. Search or use quick locate to switch focus.
explore.noMore: This entity has no further neighbors to expand
explore.viewFacts_one: View the {{count}} fact behind this relation
explore.viewFacts_other: View the {{count}} facts behind this relation
explore.showAxis: Show the {{axis}} range on the left
explore.layerBy: Spread entities into layers by the {{axis}} where they first appear
explore.layerByFollow: Spread entities into layers by first appearance (the range follows the timeline below)
explore.resetTitle: Reset the view: unpin nodes, leave focus and details, and frame the whole graph

explore.loadedNote: Showing the {{shown}} relations already on the canvas, of {{total}} in total. Use the aim button to load more.

analysis.flowSum: {{links}} flows on the canvas · {{entities}} entities · {{facts}} facts

flow.emptyHelp: This view counts relations already on the canvas: which entity, through which relation, to which entity. Search for an entity, or use Quick locate to open the event or organization library, then come back.

galaxy.hitPaged: {{total}} passages matched. Highlighted {{shown}} and moved to the first.

galaxy.overview: {{cluster}} overview · {{count}} groups (open a bubble or zoom for passages)
galaxy.unlike: Unlike the rest of its group

galaxy.driftHelp: Each step covers {{size}} {{unit}}. Watch which {{cluster}} grow, and which words appear or fade.
galaxy.reportFail: Could not export the change report
galaxy.hintSegment: Each star is one passage of the source
galaxy.hintTouch: Pinch to zoom · drag to pan
galaxy.hintMouse: Scroll to zoom · drag to pan
galaxy.hintBubble: Open a bubble to see that group
galaxy.hintDot: Open a dot for the passage
galaxy.hintCompare: Select several groups in the side list to compare
galaxy.hintMenu: The analysis menu shows links and how centers move
galaxy.clearCompare: Clear the selection and leave compare mode
galaxy.filterClusters: Filter {{cluster}} by name, summary, or frequent words
galaxy.strengthHint: Drag left to see every link, or right to keep only the tightest {{cluster}}.
galaxy.algorithmHint: The two methods draw different links. The default is usually enough.
galaxy.score: Difference {{score}} (higher means less like this group)
galaxy.noDrift: No change data yet. Reanalyze first.
galaxy.driftNote: This is how a whole span of {{axis}} is composed, not a single {{segment}} moving on the map.
galaxy.reanalyzeNote: This recomputes vectors, layout, groups, and names. It takes a minute or two, and the previous result stays visible.
galaxy.emptyGalaxy: Nothing to show yet. Run npm run kg:build {{id}}, or use the button below. Each star will be one {{segment}}, colored by its {{cluster}}.
galaxy.truncation: This view is crowded, so only the first {{limit}} {{segment}} are shown. Zoom in to see the rest.
galaxy.outlierHelp: These passages stand out in one of two ways: they read more like another {{cluster}}, or they differ from the rest of their group. Both are hints. Open the source to check.
galaxy.similarRef: Reference: {{name}} (matched by meaning, not by distance on the map)

clue.r2: {{name}} is killed by {{killer}} in {{death}}, but “{{predicate}}” still appears in {{later}}
clue.r2plain: {{name}} is killed by {{killer}} in {{death}}, yet still appears in {{later}}
clue.r3: {{name}} drops out after {{from}} and returns in {{to}} ({{gap}} {{unit}} later)
clue.m1: “{{target}}” depends on “{{prerequisite}}”, but {{prerequisite}} first appears in {{preAt}} ({{target}} is in {{targetAt}})
clue.m3: “{{name}}” appears only in {{unit}}, with no prerequisite or follow-on link
clue.m4: “{{name}}” is taught in {{from}} and not used again until “{{other}}” in {{to}}

ask.hint: Answers use only the book. Tap [n] to read the passage.

review.intro: These facts are the most likely extraction errors. Check the passage: confirm the right ones, reject the wrong ones. Rejected facts are removed from the graph.
review.readonly: Read-only: run locally or set a review token to confirm or reject.
